question: Compare units sold October 1 through 3, 2026 with stock on hand October 3, 2026 for every product.
For products sold October 1 through 3, 2026, which warehouse inventory records were below reorder point on October 3, 2026?
How much net revenue did each product generate October 1 through 3, 2026 and how many warehouses held stock on October 3, 2026?

description: Physical stock for one product at one warehouse on one snapshot date. Additive across warehouses on the same date.
SKU identifier matching the sales domain.
Warehouse-specific reorder threshold. Low stock means on_hand_units < reorder_point_units; equal is not below threshold.
Daily snapshot date. Never add stock across snapshot dates. Fixture date is 2026-10-03.

One row per snapshot date, SKU, warehouse. Select exactly one snapshot date. Aggregate to product_id before joining product-level sales; retain warehouse grain only for warehouse-specific stock flags.
Net revenue in USD, already after discounts. Sum across sale lines. Fixture excludes returns and tax.
Calendar sale date. Fixture covers October 1 through 3, 2026.
Units sold on a sale line; additive across sale lines.
One row per sale line. Historical sales flow: aggregate to product_id before joining inventory; a raw join duplicates sales across warehouses and snapshots.

question: Compare units sold October 1 through 3, 2026 with stock on hand October 3, 2026 for every product.
sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT s.product_id, s.product_name, SUM(s.units) AS units_sold FROM northstar_demo.retail.sales AS s WHERE s.sale_date BETWEEN DATE'2026-10-01' AND DATE'2026-10-03' GROUP BY s.product_id, s.product_name), stock AS (SELECT i.product_id, SUM(i.on_hand_units) AS on_hand_units FROM northstar_demo.retail.inventory AS i WHERE i.snapshot_date = DATE'2026-10-03' GROUP BY i.product_id) SELECT sold.product_id, sold.product_name, sold.units_sold, stock.on_hand_units FROM sold LEFT JOIN stock ON sold.product_id = stock.product_id ORDER BY sold.product_id LIMIT 20
usage_guidance: Explicit sales date range and single inventory snapshot; aggregate facts before joining to avoid multiplied totals.

question: For products sold October 1 through 3, 2026, which warehouse inventory records were below reorder point on October 3, 2026?
sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT s.product_id, SUM(s.units) AS units_sold FROM northstar_demo.retail.sales AS s WHERE s.sale_date BETWEEN DATE'2026-10-01' AND DATE'2026-10-03' GROUP BY s.product_id) SELECT i.product_id, i.product_name, i.warehouse, i.on_hand_units, i.reorder_point_units, sold.units_sold FROM northstar_demo.retail.inventory AS i INNER JOIN sold ON i.product_id = sold.product_id WHERE i.snapshot_date = DATE'2026-10-03' AND i.on_hand_units < i.reorder_point_units ORDER BY i.product_id, i.warehouse LIMIT 20
usage_guidance: Explicit sales date range and single inventory snapshot; aggregate facts before joining to avoid multiplied totals.

question: How much net revenue did each product generate October 1 through 3, 2026 and how many warehouses held stock on October 3, 2026?
sql: WITH revenue AS (SELECT s.product_id, s.product_name, SUM(s.net_revenue_usd) AS revenue_usd FROM northstar_demo.retail.sales AS s WHERE s.sale_date BETWEEN DATE'2026-10-01' AND DATE'2026-10-03' GROUP BY s.product_id, s.product_name), stock AS (SELECT i.product_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.warehouse) AS warehouses_with_stock FROM northstar_demo.retail.inventory AS i WHERE i.snapshot_date = DATE'2026-10-03' AND i.on_hand_units > 0 GROUP BY i.product_id) SELECT revenue.product_id, revenue.product_name, revenue.revenue_usd, stock.warehouses_with_stock FROM revenue LEFT JOIN stock ON revenue.product_id = stock.product_id ORDER BY revenue.product_id LIMIT 20
usage_guidance: Explicit sales date range and single inventory snapshot; aggregate facts before joining to avoid multiplied totals.

## DISAMBIGUATION
- Ask for a historical sales period or inventory snapshot date when missing; do not describe the October 2026 fixture as current live data.

## Instructions you must follow when providing summaries
- State the sales date range and inventory snapshot date separately.
- Distinguish observed low stock from a purchase recommendation; this agent has no supplier lead-time or replenishment-policy source.
